blocked.mathematical_obstruction: The full consumer entails bull-free Berge perfection. Given any bull-free Berge H, add a universal vertex u to H, then take disjoint union with C5. Adding u preserves bull-freeness (u cannot be a pendant, and any two prospective pendants inside H are adjacent to u); the H+u component remains Berge. Every odd hole/antihole in the disjoint union lies in C5 and has no complete outside witness, so the graph is basic. Its neighborhood at u is H and antineighborhood is C5, which is not perfect. Thus the unchanged consumer forces H perfect. A bipartite/chordal special-case proof cannot preserve the full claim.
